These spirits spend most of their time in their vessel-like dwellings. But when the elements are put in balance, the spirits emerge from their vessels and show themselves in their full form. Each spirit embodies one of the four elements and influences the harmony between them. In Sagani, as you and your opponents create this colorful, harmonious world by employing your Sound discs, the spirits become fully visible. Every spirit that shows itself also brings you a step closer to victory. Number of players: 1 - 4 Game duration: 23 mn Complexity: 3 / 5 Play Sagani and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Overview Each tile is one of four colors (four elements). Each tile has arrows in the same four colors. The aim is to places tiles so the arrows correctly point to tiles in matching colors -- without having too many incomplete. Turn On your turn, take a tile and place it in your area abutting pre-existing ones in whichever orientation you wish. If there's only one tile left, you can choose to take it or put it into Intermezzo and take the one at the top of the draw deck. Stack " sound discs " on the new tile equal to the number of arrows it displays. If you do not have enough sound discs, the remaining must be made up of " cacophony discs " (which are bad and cost negative 2 points). However, you should first check to see if you can recover any discs by covering the last arrow on another tile on your personal display (keep reading, you'll understand better in a second). This may save you from having to take Cacophony discs! An arrow is fulfilled when it points to a tile of the same color as itself (this doesn't have to be adjacent directly, just in that required line of sight). When this happens, a sound disc moves onto the arrow to show it is fulfilled. If all the arrows on a tile are now covered, this tile is complete and now scores. Take back all the Discs from it and flip it. Check if Intermezzo is now full or not (4 tiles). If Intermezzo is full, each player can take one tile from those available. Players get to claim tiles in reverse order of " harmony " score. If no one takes anything, all are discarded. After this, check the Offer Display, if there are 0 tiles, refill with 5, otherwise they stay as they are Game End The game ends when someone reaches or exceeds 75/60/45 points in a 2/3/4 player game. Keep going until all players have had an equal number of turns If the draw stack has less or equal than 4 cards left. The game will end with the last player in turn order Whoever has the most points after this wins If there's a tie, the player who reached that many points first (i.e. is lower in the stack) wins Board Game Arena would like to thank Skellig Games for making it possible to have this game here. 1783 sagani العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 1/10] What feels just like a lighter version of habitats. Does away with the moving around a pawn to collect and the tile conditions are easier to satisfy. Overall an enjoyable refinement to the genre without really introducing anything new or groundbreaking. Would make a great starting point for someone without habitats or nova luna.

[Rating: 2/10] I was really hoping to like Sagani since I love tile laying games and the art is cute, but I just didn't find it fun. It's a very multi-solitaire feeling game, everyone is taking care of their own play area and there isn't much interaction and it depends on luck.?

[Rating: 3/10] What a frustrating gaming experience this has been for me. If the colors you need to finish of tiles don't come out, you're screwed big time. The complete game felt like a complete crapshoot to me. Once you're in trouble, you'll likely be in trouble for the remainder of the game. Never had such a bad experience with a Rosenberg-game before :'(

[Rating: 3/10] I didn't like having so few choices and so little planning possible.  Only seeing four tiles at a time is very frustrating and you can just get completely shut out of a color you desperately need.  I enjoy Nova Luna a lot more than this.

[Rating: 3/10] Mag gut sein, wenn man es aus dem Bauch heraus spielen kann. Wer es wie wir kompetitiv spielt (ich möchte gewinnen), kommt nicht drumherum jede Option zu durchdenken, was ewig dauert und Downtimes erzeugt, die keinen Spaß mehr machen. Eine Partie dauerte bei uns 1,5h (mit 2 Spieler!) - da kann ich auch etwas epischeres für die Zeit spielen.  Für uns hat das Spiel pro Zug leider zu viel Optionen und daher schon beinahe den Schach-Effekt.  Das Spiel ist nicht schlecht, aber spielen möchte ich es nicht mehr.

[Rating: 3/10] Quality game. Well designed, artwork could be better. Need more plays. Tile placement. Interesting and simple introductory game.

[Rating: 3/10] Played solo a bunch on BGA. With other players and drafting the experience is probably better, but I really don't enjoy playing with rando's on the internet.  The solo experience seemed cool and puzzly at first, but after 10 games or so it became clear that drawing the right tile at the right time makes this a cakewalk or a grueling slog through the jungle of un-fun.  I had two games where there wasn't a single white tile in the first 25 drawn.  The score reached -40.  At that point why bother playing?

[Rating: 3/10] After 1 play on BGA: It’s an interesting concept that the arrows can extend over any number of cards. Still, it's not for me. There’s a whole bunch of games where you have to sort cards while respecting their order. At first, things go fairly well, but toward the end, it gradually falls apart. So I spend most of the game just hoping it will hold together for as long as possible… until the inevitable happens and I don’t gain the points I was aiming for. Avoiding damage under constant tension — all in all, that’s not a game experience I find particularly enjoyable.

[Rating: 3/10] More of the same.  I'm shocked by how a fanous designer can create a boring game like this, just for money. It's just like using his fanbase to give them a junk game, thinking "they are stupid, they will still buy it and call it a great game".
